text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager alert: Dedicated reserved pool 'qc-resv-us-east-2' at 99% GPU utilization. Queue growth observed for multiple enterprise tenants; QuantumCity showing highest error rate (503). Escalating to SRE on-call @eva_oncall.

eva_oncall: ack — joining. pulling live metrics and autoscaler logs.

ben_runtime: looking at autoscaler: controllers report repeated CreateInstance errors -> "quota_exceeded" and "rate_limit" from cloud provider. Autoscaler attempted scale-up 6x in last 10m.

dmitri_ml: QuantumCity workload looks like long-context interactive sessions with sustained KV-cache writes. A few sessions are holding large KV caches causing eviction pressure and kernel OOMs on some infer nodes.

carla_cs: QuantumCity support: customers seeing high latency and 503s since ~13:45 PT, some report retries making it worse. I opened QC ticket #QC-487 and pinged their infra lead.

eva_oncall: action plan: 1) try quick noisy-session eviction, 2) route QuantumCity to fallback pool if available, 3) reduce per-request max_context for QC temporarily. Starting eviction now.

frank_ops: running eviction command ->
```
# internal ops tool
opsctl evict-sessions --pool qc-resv-us-east-2 --predicate "owner:quantumcity and active_tokens>200" --max-terminate 250
```

frank_ops: eviction started. terminating 162 sessions owned by QuantumCity (priority noisy sessions). :wrench:

ben_runtime: autoscaler note: cloud quota still blocking new GPU creations. We can route to resv-us-west-1 if that pool has spare capacity; creating routing rule requires a small config change.

eva_oncall: frank/frank_ops — can you spin traffic to fallback? If not available, reduce model size for QC traffic to conserve GPUs.

frank_ops: attempting route update ->
```
infractl route-tenant --tenant quantumcity --from-pool qc-resv-us-east-2 --to-pool resv-us-west-1 --dry-run
infractl apply-route --tenant quantumcity --to-pool resv-us-west-1
```

frank_ops: applied route, starting nw drain on us-east tasks for QC.

ben_runtime: queue length dropped from ~480 to ~120 within 90s after eviction + routing. CPU/GPU load on us-east nodes decreased. But cloud API still returning quota_exceeded on scale attempts — need quota bump for sustained recovery.

dmitri_ml: I pushed a temporary inference-config override for QC to cap context_length=2048 and enable KV compression flag. That cut median token usage by ~35%.

carla_cs: Notified QuantumCity: told them we performed emergency evictions and routed traffic to fallback region; they see improvement but asked for timeline. Shared ticket #QC-487.

eva_oncall: current status: customer-facing impact reduced to degraded (some increased latency) not complete outage. Autoscaler blocked by cloud quota; ops to request quota increase and we should schedule postmortem.

frank_ops: raised cloud quota request (CR-9421) and flagged enterprise priority. Also created an internal follow-up to add noisy-session detection to the autoscale policy.

ben_runtime: noted root causes: (1) noisy long-lived sessions from QuantumCity, (2) autoscaler throttled by cloud API rate/quotas, (3) no automatic fallback routing when scale fails. Recommend immediate TODOs: quota increase, add fallback routing circuit, add per-tenant session caps, add autoscaler retry/backoff improvements.

dmitri_ml: will add a regression test with synthetic QC-style workload to the ci/inference-load suite.

eva_oncall: thanks team. I'll keep this thread open for the on-call handoff. Current timeline: impact contained. Next steps: handoff to morning SRE (Ben) for follow-up + postmortem.

carla_cs: I'll coordinate the customer update and follow-up SLA credit discussion if needed.

incident-bot: oncall handoff scheduled: eva_oncall -> ben_runtime at 08:00 UTC. Incident severity downgraded to Sev-2 at 14:10 PT.

frank_ops: adding runbook note: "If dedicated pool scale attempts fail with quota_exceeded, route high-impact tenants to fallback pool and evict noisy sessions. Open cloud quota ticket and notify account team."

eva_oncall: closing active mitigation. leaving a summary in #postmortems and will kick off postmortem doc tomorrow. Good job everyone. :white_check_mark:
